g.text: because they call for three different actions):
remembered path empty -> select page, "none run yet"
load fails -> select page, "could not be loaded: <reason>"
load succeeds -> runtime view, tasks already running
The remembered path is written ONLY after a load
succeeds, so a corrupt file never becomes the one
Tasks enter runtime with no button press. A task that
fails setup keeps its tile showing Faulted, and tasks
past the 8 cap are named in the log and toolbar --
a task nobody can see is a task nobody is watching.
ADS has docking and floating but no "tile into N"
primitive, so the grid is an explicit sequence of
Floating is an operator decision and is never undone
by a layout change: a floated dock is skipped and
does not consume a tile. Floating is a VIEW
operation -- a floated task keeps running.
Phase 6 split the product into two shells by the
project owner's decision, superseding the Phase 4
They are PEERS over the same src/ modules, not a
hierarchy: neither may include the other's headers.
Shared qmake config lives in qmake/app_common.pri.
Only this shell writes a project file. One writer,
one reader -- which is why no project-file
compatibility layer between them is needed.
